Deconstruct Revenue Rises 30 Percent to Rs 165 Cr in FY26

Bengaluru-based direct-to-consumer (D2C) skincare brand Deconstruct reported revenue of Rs 165 crore in FY26, marking a 30 percent year-on-year increase from Rs 127 crore in FY25. The company's operating revenue has grown 25-fold over three years, although higher expenditure on marketing and business operations pushed it into a net loss of Rs 5.4 crore during the financial year ended March 2026.

Deconstruct continued to expand its business while maintaining a relatively limited loss compared with its revenue. However, the company's total expenses increased faster than its revenue, affecting its overall profitability. [...] Following the latest investment, Drivn Transition PTE. LTD, the Singapore-based parent company, continues to hold a majority stake of 88.75 percent in the Indian business. Avaana Capital now owns 7.22 percent, while co-founder and Chief Executive Officer Manav Bansal holds 4.03 percent.

Despite securing funding and attracting strategic backing, the Indian entity remained at a pre-revenue stage during FY26. Regulatory filings show that the company reported a loss of Rs 1.96 crore during the financial year as it continued to invest in building its operations and platform capabilities. [...] Apart from Xponentia Capital, Traya's investors include Kae Capital, Fireside Ventures and Whiteboard Capital.

The company has yet to file its financial statements for the financial year 2025-26 (FY26) with the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA). Its operating revenue increased 43 percent year-on-year to Rs 338.4 crore in FY25, compared with Rs 236 crore in FY24.

Despite the revenue growth, Traya reported a net loss of Rs 22.5 crore in FY25, against a profit of Rs 8.8 crore in the previous financial year. Its total expenses rose 60 percent year-on-year to Rs 365.5 crore during the period.
